tips: Review your cancellation policy every quarter against what competitors nearby are offering.
A five-minute daily huddle with front-of-house catches small problems before they become reviews.
Track your no-show rate by booking channel — it varies more than most operators expect.
Ask returning guests one open question at check-out; the answers are your best market research.
Audit your listing photos twice a year — tired images quietly suppress conversion on OTAs.
Small upgrades offered at check-in convert better than the same upgrade offered by email in advance.
Slow midweek nights respond better to added value than to discounting the headline rate.
Respond to every review, good or bad, within 48 hours — response rate is itself a trust signal.
Keep a running list of guest requests you had to say no to; it's your best product roadmap.
Staff turnover costs more in service consistency than in recruitment fees — factor both in.
quotes: A guest remembers how the stay felt long after they forget what it cost.
Consistency is a quieter kind of hospitality, but it's the one guests come back for.
The room sells the first night. The service sells the return visit.
Every empty room tonight is a decision made weeks ago, not a surprise today.
Good hospitality notices what a guest didn't ask for.
A small hotel run well beats a large hotel run adequately.
The best reviews are written about staff, not amenities.
Price is what's on the tariff. Value is what the guest tells their friends.
Occupancy fills rooms. Reputation fills them at the rate you actually want.
The first ninety seconds of check-in set the tone for the whole stay.
salesIdeas: Bundle a late check-out with your lowest midweek rate band to lift perceived value without cutting price.
Offer a small local-produce hamper as a paid add-on — low cost, high margin, and supports local suppliers.
Create a 'stay and dine' rate combining a room with a fixed-price dinner during quiet weeknights.
Test a direct-booking discount clearly flagged against your OTA rate to nudge channel mix.
Package your dish and drink of the day as a welcome offer for guests booking direct.
Offer a short-notice upgrade rate by text to guests already checked in, rather than at booking.
Run a loyalty perk for guests who've stayed three times, even if it's small — recognition outperforms discounts.
Partner with a nearby attraction for a joint ticket-plus-room package during shoulder season.
Add a late-availability rate visible only in the last 48 hours before arrival to capture last-minute demand.
Highlight your seasonal menu on the booking confirmation email — it's an underused upsell moment.
